memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The same law applies to everyone who sins unintentionally, whether a native-born Israelite or a foreigner residing among you. But anyone who sins defiantly, whether native-born or foreigner, blasphemes the Lord and must be cut off from the people of Israel. Because they have despised the Lord's word and broken his commands, they must surely be cut off; their guilt remains on them.'" — Num 15:29-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here Scripture draws an important line. There is a difference between sinning "unintentionally" and sinning "defiantly" — literally, "with a high hand." One is the stumble of a person who wants to please God but fails; the other is the raised fist of someone who knowingly shakes it at God and despises His word. God treats these very differently.

We should not soften this hard passage. Defiant, deliberate sin — sin that scorns God and refuses to repent — is a grave thing. The person here is not struggling and falling; they are proudly rejecting God's authority and treasuring their rebellion. Such an attitude, left unrepented, cuts a person off from the life of God's people. This is a sobering warning against a hardened, unrepentant heart.

But we must read this carefully. The passage is not describing the believer who battles sin and grieves over their failures — that person is covered, as the previous verses made so clear. It describes the one who defiantly despises God's word and will not turn. The issue is the posture of the heart: humble and repentant, or proud and defiant.

This searches us. Do we treasure any sin, clinging to it and refusing to let God address it? The gospel calls us not to a life free of stumbling, but to a life of ongoing repentance, never nursing rebellion in our hearts. And here is the wonder: even defiant sinners like us have hope, because Christ bore the very guilt that "remains" on the unrepentant. The high-handed sin that should cut us off was laid on Him. The door of repentance stands open — do not harden your heart, but come.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What is the difference between stumbling in sin and defying God in sin?
2. Is there any sin you are treasuring rather than repenting of?
3. How does Christ bearing our guilt open the door for even defiant sinners?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep my heart soft and repentant, never proud and defiant against Your word. Show me any sin I am clinging to, and help me to turn from it. Thank You that Christ bore the guilt that should have cut me off. Amen.
